source_text: Τοὺς δὲ οἴκοις ἀλλοτρίοις ἐπελθεῖν τολμήσαντας, ἐὰν μὲν κατηγορηθέντες ἐλεγχθῶσι, μηδὲ τῆς ἀκροάσεως ἀξιώσῃς, ἐὰν δὲ ἑαυτοὺς ἐξείπωσι καὶ ἀποδῶσιν, ἐν τῇ τῶν ὑποστρεφόντων τάξει ὑποπίπτειν.
thought_title: Treatment of those who entered strangers' houses during the invasion
orientation: Gregory continues his pastoral instructions to the bishop, now addressing a third category of offenders: those who dared enter houses not their own during the barbarian incursion, with different outcomes depending on whether they are convicted or confess.
pass_a_gloss: But those who dared to enter houses not their own, if indeed having been accused they should be convicted, not even of the hearing may you deem worthy; but if they should confess themselves and give account, to fall in among the order of those who are returning.

lemmas.gloss: belonging to another, not one's own (dative plural)
to enter, come upon (aorist active infinitive)
having dared (aorist active participle accusative plural masculine)
having been accused (aorist passive participle nominative plural masculine)
they should be convicted / found guilty (aorist passive subjunctive 3rd plural)
you may deem worthy (aorist active subjunctive 2nd singular)
they should confess / speak out fully (aorist active subjunctive 3rd plural)
they should give account / render (aorist active subjunctive 3rd plural)

choices.why: Glossary does not lock this phrase; literal rendering captures the dative of place with 'ἐπελθεῖν' and the sense of entering another's property.
Aorist infinitive + aorist participle shows the boldness of the completed action; 'dared' preserves the volitional nuance of τολμάω.

choices.english: having been accused they should be convicted
choices.why: Two distinct stages: passive participle for the accusation, subjunctive for the judicial conviction; keeps the legal sequence clear.
rejected: if they are accused and found guilty

choices.why: ἐξέω = speak out fully, confess; ἀποδίδωμι = render, give back, here 'give account of oneself'. Both aorist subjunctives parallel the condition.

choices.form: ἐν τῇ τῶν ὑποστρεφόντων τάξει ὑποπίπτειν
choices.english: to fall in among the order of those who are returning
choices.why: Táxis = ordered group; ὑποστρέφω = turn back/return (from captivity or apostasy); ὑποπίπτω = fall under, be placed in. Present infinitive shows the ongoing status.
rejected: to be ranked among the returning
to join the company of those turning back
to be classed with the returnees

pass_b_english: If you find that those who dared to enter houses not their own have been accused and convicted, you must not even admit them to the rank of hearers. But if they confess themselves and make restitution, they are to be placed in the order of those who are returning.

problems.why: Here ἀποδῶσιν means to give back or make restitution for what was taken, not to give an account. The English loses the requirement to return stolen goods.
problems.fix: But if they confess of their own accord and make restitution

problems.quote: you must not even grant them a hearing
problems.why: ἀκρόασις is the penitential rank of 'hearers', who may listen to the Scriptures being read. A 'hearing' suggests a trial, which misleads the reader.
problems.fix: you must not even admit them to the rank of hearers
problems.ruling: ἀκροάσεως is the hearers' penitential rank; 'grant a hearing' reads as trial, clashing with ἐλεγχθῶσι and τάξει ὑποστρεφόντων.

edits.old: you must not even grant them a hearing
edits.new: you must not even admit them to the rank of hearers

edits.old: But if they confess themselves and give a full account
edits.new: But if they confess themselves and make restitution

fixed: 'give a full account' -> 'make restitution': ἀποδῶσιν means give back/make restitution for what was taken in others' houses, not give an account.
'grant them a hearing' -> 'admit them to the rank of hearers': μηδὲ τῆς ἀκροάσεως ἀξιώσῃς refers to the penitential rank of hearers, not a trial hearing.
